explanation: In Singapore, beckoning someone with a curled index finger is considered impolite and condescending, as it is associated with calling a dog or a servant. This gesture is seen as disrespectful, especially in a multicultural society where maintaining face and showing mutual respect are highly valued. A more acceptable way to summon someone is to use an open hand with a gentle waving motion.
local_tip: Instead of using your finger, wave your hand with the palm facing down and fingers together to beckon someone politely.
regional_note: Among older generations and in traditional Chinese families, this gesture is particularly offensive, while younger Singaporeans may be more tolerant but still view it as rude.

also_check.note: Beckoning with a finger is considered vulgar and is used only for animals; use an open hand with palm down instead.
This gesture can be seen as a challenge or insult, and may even lead to legal trouble if used toward authorities.
While often used informally among friends, it can be perceived as arrogant or dismissive in formal or professional settings.
